clue.text: Asians not the first to see Naples on tour

indicators.note: on tour suggests travelling around, so the letters wander into a new order
not the first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word see

explanation.surface: Tourists from Asia get a glimpse of Naples on their travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' cuts SEE to EE; 'on tour' then scrambles EE with NAPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Nepal are Asians, so this plural noun names a group of them.

clue.text: Diarist lacking in substance

parts.note: lacking something means having no amount of it
body is substance, as in a wine with plenty of body

explanation.surface: A diary writer whose life has little to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody, by George and Weedon Grossmith, is the comic journal of the clerk Charles Pooter; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional author of The Diary of a Nobody is a diarist known by that title word.

clue.text: European clear in athletic event

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland
to vault is to clear an obstacle by jumping

explanation.surface: A European athlete clears the bar at a track meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is a field event in athletics, jumping a bar with a long pole.

clue.text: Launch from lake, provided the swell ends

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
a toff is a swell, an upper-class dandy in British slang, and he ends the word

explanation.surface: A boat is pushed out from the shore, provided the waves die down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like a wave on the lake, but here it is a smart, upper-class man, a TOFF in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A liftoff is the launch of a rocket or aircraft as it leaves the ground.

clue.text: Barges bully on board

indicators.note: on here means aboard, so the bullying word is placed within the ship

parts.note: board stands for a ship, SS, the abbreviation for steamship, as in going on board
to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them

explanation.surface: Bargemen push around a fellow crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: the piece goes inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat, a kind of barge used for cargo.

clue.text: Conflict in the plant not unrestricted at first

indicators.note: not tells us a part of the plant's name is to be removed
at first places the removed part at the beginning of the plant's name

parts.note: loosestrife is a flowering plant, such as purple loosestrife
loose means unrestricted, free of ties

explanation.surface: Trouble in the factory unless the reins are kept tight from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory but is a flower: LOOSESTRIFE loses LOOSE from its front, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement, a synonym for conflict or discord.

clue.text: Bet on first in Derby produced twice as much again

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts one piece placed after the other

parts.note: a treble is a bet on three races, the winnings rolled from one to the next

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word Derby

explanation.surface: A punter's bet on the Derby favourite pays off handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, which fits the betting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To treble is to multiply by three, giving twice as much again on top of the original.

clue.text: Lazy person unravelled riddle half-heartedly

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled, so the letters are rearranged
half-heartedly removes half of the doubled letter at the heart of riddle

explanation.surface: Someone too lazy to work out a puzzle properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' loses one of the two middle Ds of RIDDLE, giving RIDLE, which 'unravelled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who idles, avoiding work: a lazy person or loafer.

clue.text: Always make arrangement for remover to take a key

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: making an arrangement of something suggests reordering it, here the letters of remover

explanation.surface: Someone is forever booking the removal men and getting a key cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link; 'make arrangement for' scrambles the letters of 'remover', placed after the musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is a poetic word for forever or for all time, the same as always.

clue.text: Pull up abruptly — terminus no longer in use

parts.note: a stop is a terminus or halting place for a bus or train
dead means defunct, no longer in use, as in a dead language

explanation.surface: A train halts sharply at a disused end-of-line station.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop dead is an idiom for halting suddenly and completely.

clue.text: Sprint by university athlete in unexpected event

parts.note: to bolt is to sprint away suddenly
a Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman, so something made by one comes from the Blue

explanation.surface: A college runner's dash produces a shock result.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt from the blue is an idiom for a sudden shock, like lightning out of a clear sky.

clue.text: Going astray in roundabout

definitions.meaning: deviating from the right path or course, in an old sense
indirect, not straightforward, as a roundabout route

explanation.definitionFit: Devious means departing from the direct way, either wandering off course or being indirect.

clue.text: Impudent talk rebuffed by sinister traveller

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests something pushed back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: lip is cheeky or impudent talk
grim means sinister or forbidding

explanation.surface: A wanderer rejects some cheek from a menacing stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a traveller, especially one journeying to a holy place.

clue.text: Vote for unpolished man of wisdom, as Spooner might put it

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: rough means unpolished, crude
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Supporting a crude philosopher at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of ROUGH SAGE gives 'suff rage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage is the right to vote in elections, or a vote itself.

clue.text: Orchid like this in size

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the word for size

parts.note: area is a measure of size, as of a room
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A flower described as being about this big.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa is a genus of North American orchid, the bog rose, named after a nymph.

clue.text: Play for time in game without mid-off

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places one piece around the other

parts.note: deer are game animals, hunted for sport
the middle of the word off is the letter F

explanation.surface: Stalling in a cricket match that lacks a fielder at mid-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here it means the middle letter of 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone, putting something off to gain time.

clue.text: Mercenary journalist?

definitions.meaning: a ... was a medieval knight who sold his services to any lord
a writer selling work to several papers rather than one employer

explanation.definitionFit: A freelance originally meant a hired soldier and now means a self-employed writer or worker.

clue.text: Unsophisticated joke by detective in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as said aloud, the spoken sound of the name

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes is the famous fictional detective
a pun is a joke playing on words

explanation.surface: A simple gag from a sleuth chatting away.
explanation.walkthrough: The name HOLMES is pronounced without its L, like 'homes'; 'by' joins PUN alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and simple, unsophisticated, like cloth spun at home.

clue.text: Eye kept on the consumption of drink

definitions.text: Eye kept on the consumption of drink

parts.words: Eye kept on the consumption of drink
parts.note: a device on an upturned spirits bottle in a pub measures each shot, like an eye monitoring how much is poured; also simply relating to the eye

explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs this is the measuring gadget fixed to a bottle; the word also means relating to sight.

clue.text: The food is in copper ewer initially, cooking

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of ewer

explanation.surface: A meal is being prepared in a copper pot with a jug beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The food' describes the dish being made; 'cooking' is the definition, a style of cookery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cooking, the characteristic food of a place.

clue.text: Shuffling about, and green may be put at risk

indicators.note: shuffling about mixes up the order, here of the letters

explanation.surface: Moving around carelessly on the golf green could put things in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose to harm or danger, putting something at risk.

clue.text: One likely to be bowled over by cheese

definitions.text: One likely to be bowled over by cheese

parts.words: One likely to be bowled over by cheese
parts.note: in skittles the heavy disc thrown at the pins is called a cheese, so a pin is knocked down by it

explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is an old British pub game in which a wooden disc called a cheese is thrown at nine pins.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is a skittle, one of the nine pins knocked down in the game.

clue.text: Employer admitted the game's up as a money-lender

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a user is one who employs or makes use of something

indicators.note: is up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A boss confesses the game is over, posing as a loan shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the game's up' reads like a confession, but the game is rugby union, and ''s up' turns it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, a money-lender.

clue.text: American side used such language!

definitions.meaning: in American billiards and pool, side is spin put on the ball

explanation.definitionFit: English is the American term for sidespin on a ball, and also a language.

clue.text: Cat-like French playwright

definitions.meaning: a small cat-like carnivore related to the civet
Jean ... wrote The Maids and The Balcony

explanation.definitionFit: A genet is a civet-like mammal, and Genet was a French dramatist.

clue.text: Kindly beginning to supply maggots

parts.note: gentle means kindly, tender

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of supply

explanation.surface: A kindly person starts handing out maggots.
explanation.walkthrough: Gentles are maggots used by British anglers as fishing bait.
explanation.definitionFit: In angling, gentles is the name for blowfly larvae, maggots used as bait.

clue.text: Collect spoken in African republic

indicators.note: spoken means said aloud, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to garner is to collect or gather

explanation.surface: A collection is spoken of in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent without the R, GARNER sounds like the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a republic in West Africa, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Device used by writers to make point

definitions.text: Device used by writers to make point

parts.words: Device used by writers to make point
parts.note: writers might make a point in an argument, but this gadget sharpens their pencils to a point

explanation.definitionFit: This small tool puts a sharp tip on a pencil for anyone who writes.

clue.text: Bag lady's used Underground

parts.note: to net is to bag or catch
her means belonging to a lady

explanation.surface: A woman's bag was used on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube; here it means lower or below.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or underneath, as in the nether regions below ground.

clue.text: In general, use this protection in case of a fall

definitions.text: In general, use this protection in case of a fall

parts.words: In general, use this protection in case of a fall
parts.note: a fall here is of rain, not a tumble, so the protection is clothing worn against the weather

explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof clothing worn in wet weather protects against a fall of rain.
